title: Doroni Aerospace surpasses $60 million raised
summary: Doroni is building the H1-X personal flying vehicle.
body_markdown:
[Doroni Aerospace](https://doroni.io/) , the Florida flying car company building the H1-X personal flying vehicle, announced it has raised more than $60 million from more than 20,000 investors across its community-backed rounds.


Doroni plans to put the new capital directly toward hiring engineers, expanding key partnerships, and begin preparations for advanced test flights of the H1-X in 2027.


This extraordinary milestone arrives at a moment when flying cars continue to grow in global popularity. In October, Tesla unveiled its next-generation Roadster as a car that can fly using thruster technology to lift the vehicle into the air during a livestreamed demonstration in Texas.


For Doroni, this achievement confirms what its founders and investors have believed for years: People are ready for the next era of personal mobility.


“When the most famous carmaker on earth starts talking about flying cars, the whole world starts imagining what’s possible,” said Doron Merdinger, founder and CEO of Doroni Aerospace.


“That’s great for everyone who shares this vision. Our investors saw it early, and they’re the reason we’re building it today. A hundred years ago, the car gave people the freedom to go anywhere the road could take them. Our vision is to give people the sky. Ten years from now, I believe flying your own aircraft to work, to the beach, or to see family will feel as normal as driving does today. Every engineer we hire and every test we run is a step toward that world.”


Doroni’s long-term vision is a world no longer limited by roads — where people can rise above traffic patterns, reach places faster, see the world from above, and spend more of their time doing what they love.


Over the next decade, Doroni plans to make personal flight a natural part of everyday life, the same way the automobile reshaped the 20th century.


The company sees this as a natural evolution: Electric vehicles proved the drivetrain, drones proved the flight profile, and advanced carbon fiber proved the structure. Doroni is bringing those breakthroughs together into one aircraft designed for individuals and families.


The company plans to pursue that vision in clear stages: Complete the H1-X engineering program, fly its prototype through an advanced test campaign beginning in 2027, advance through light-sport aircraft certification under the FAA’s new MOSAIC rule, and then scale manufacturing and a nationwide service network.


“We are pursuing this vision in clear, deliberate stages,” said Rami Arbili, COO at Doroni Aerospace. “First, we will complete the H1-X engineering program, then build and take our prototype into an advanced test campaign beginning in 2027. From there, we will advance through light-sport aircraft certification under the FAA’s new MOSAIC rule before scaling manufacturing and building out a nationwide service network.”


The H1-X is designed as a two-seat personal flying vehicle with tandem wings and distributed electric propulsion. Doroni plans for it to:


- Take off and land vertically from private property where local rules permit, existing helipads, and vertiports
- Fit in a standard two-car garage and taxi out quietly on electric wheel motors
- Charge at the same fast chargers electric cars use, reaching 80 percent in about 25 minutes
- Feature SOUL AI, Doroni’s intelligent digital co-pilot, designed to assist pilots, simplify flight operations, and reduce pilot workload.
- Include a whole-airframe ballistic parachute and ten independent motors, engineered to maintain controlled flight even in the event of a single motor failure.


Doroni’s earlier prototypes have completed more than 70 test flights, including one of the first manned test flights of its kind in the United States.


The company also obtained an FAA Special Airworthiness Certificate for prototype testing. This year, Doroni signed an agreement with SES AI to supply batteries for its flying prototype and partnered with TLG Aerospace to advance the H1-X’s structural, aerodynamic, and certification engineering.


The H1-X has also drawn more than 600 pre-orders.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Doroni Aerospace.*
